A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UV-model study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–G are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original UV-model simulations and FCN, CNN and ResNet training experiments on image and synthetic datasets.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulations and neural-network experiments, including additional Transformer results on WikiText-2, initialization controls and correlation measurements.

M1.justification: The UV architecture, parameterization, GD update equations (1)–(2), fixed-point approach and EoS map (3) remain unchanged. Newly evaluated architectures and initialization variants are experimental extensions, not revisions to the proposed analytical method.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix D.3 and Figure 14 add Transformer language-model experiments on WikiText-2 using cross-entropy, substantially extending coverage beyond v1's image and synthetic-data experiments with MSE. The existing image, random, power-law, teacher-student and generative datasets remain represented.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks a proposed algorithm against competing methods. The additional NTP, initialization and LayerNorm variants serve as experimental controls for the dynamical analysis; no competing-method baseline is introduced or removed.

E3.justification: The CNN/ResNet bifurcation experiments change from width 64, 5,000 examples and SGD with batch size 512 in v1 Figures 22–23 to width 32, 1,000 examples and GD in v2 Figures 26–27. v2 Figure 4 reports stopping at 99% training accuracy, whereas v1 Figure 7 used 10,000 steps; v2 Appendix B.3 inconsistently retains the old description. New experiments also introduce cross-entropy evaluation, test-accuracy measurements and initialization/LayerNorm controls.

E4.justification: v2 adds an SP/NTP consistency check (Appendix D.1), a zero-last-layer initialization intervention (E.1, Figure 19), and quantitative sharpness–weight-norm correlation analysis (Figure 16). Figure 14 additionally compares Transformers with and without the final LayerNorm. These extend the tests of parameterization dependence and proposed mechanisms beyond v1's retained batch-size and data-correlation analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix E introduces cumulative Pearson-correlation estimation over training steps (Equation 45, Figure 16), supplementing v1's qualitative trajectory comparisons. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds Transformer training/test-loss and sharpness curves, an EoS/test-accuracy association, numerical weight-norm correlations, and the reported elimination of early sharpness reduction under zero-last-layer initialization. CNN/ResNet bifurcation trajectories and spectra are also replaced under changed settings, so their numerical differences are not same-setting performance gains. The central UV-model findings remain.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 supplies an explicit algebraic derivation of the closed function-space dynamics from GD updates. The fixed points, stability eigenvalues, critical learning rate and chaos-map conclusions are retained. The attractor analysis in C.7 already appeared in v1 Section 5.2.1.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that the UV model reproduces the four training regimes, fixed-point analysis explains their mechanisms, and initialization and parameterization govern EoS behavior. The abstract's added initialization/parameterization contribution was already explicit in v1 Section 1.1; additional experiments mainly support retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains UV-model failures concerning continued loss reduction at EoS and loss catapults at effective width one, and qualifies extension to nonlinear networks through the difficulty of closing their dynamics. Section 6.1 adds an implicit low-sharpness-bias interpretation, while Section 6.3 connects EoS to test accuracy. These substantially expand v1's interpretation and limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit NTP scaling instructions, newly specifies width 200 for the retained FCN correlation experiment, and estimates total computation below 600 A100-hours (Appendix B.6). Its new reproducibility statement says supplementary JAX code is supplied; the PDFs alone do not verify that code's accessibility.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands distinctions from Agarwala et al., Chen and Bruna, Song and Yun, and Chen et al., particularly concerning parameterization, matrix-factorization equivalence and bifurcation diagrams. v2 also adds Kong and Tao and Noci et al., introduces cited challenges to sharpness–generalization links, and removes the earlier Roberts/Yaida parameterization discussion.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the introduction, related-work discussion and conclusion, expands and renames Section 2, and reorganizes Sections 5–6. Technical attractor material and the principal weight-norm discussion move into expanded appendices. This is substantial narrative restructuring despite retention of the core theory.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column conference layout. UV and weight-norm figures move to appendices, and the fixed-point tables are consolidated. Figure 1 changes axis presentation and adds stability thresholds; the phase diagram gains accuracy panels, and new NTP, Transformer, correlation and initialization-control figures are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through initialization controls and quantified correlations, extends validation to WikiText-2/cross-entropy, and states concrete limitations of the retained UV theory. These improve support and calibration of the paper's conclusions. The gains are tempered by sparse Transformer setup details and the unresolved conflict between Figure 4's 99%-accuracy stopping rule and Appendix B.3's 10,000-step description.
